# Breusch-Pagan LM test for random effects

<small>Source: [`man/performBPRandomEffectsTest.Rd`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/heteroTests/blob/main/man/performBPRandomEffectsTest.Rd) · Help: `?performBPRandomEffectsTest`</small>

Lagrange Multiplier test for the presence of a random individual effect in panel data. This is not a test for heteroscedasticity and does not respond to one; use the auxiliary-regression diagnostics for that.

## Usage

```r
performBPRandomEffectsTest(model, data = NULL, id)
```

## Arguments

`model`
:   an object of class `lm`, the pooled `lm()` of the panel; its observations may be in any order.

`data`
:   The data frame `model` was fitted to, holding the individual identifier named by `id`, or `NULL`, the default. The residuals and weights are read from the fit itself, and `id` from the rows of `data` that hold the observations of the fit. Without `data` it is read from the model frame of `model`, which holds it only when it is a variable of the model under its own name (`id`, not `factor(id)`); an identifier the model does not use needs `data`. Since 0.16.0, data that are given are matched to the observations of the fit: rows with row names of their own by name, in any order; rows that only number themselves (a tibble, a data.table, a data frame whose row names were reset) by the row numbers of the fit, or in the order of the fit when they hold one row per observation. The rows the fit dropped may be there or not. Data whose rows cannot be shown to hold the observations of the fit are refused; see [`test_results`](test_results.md).

`id`
:   individual identifier column.

## Value

An object of class `htest`.

## Details

The statistic is Breusch and Pagan (1980) equation 5, \(LM = nT / (2(T-1)) [ \sum_i (\sum_t e_{it})^2 / \sum_{it} e_{it}^2 - 1 ]^2\), which follows a chi-square distribution with one degree of freedom under the null of no individual effect. The bracketed ratio is close to one under the null and the statistic measures its squared departure from one. Before 0.11.0 the "- 1" and the square were absent and the scaling used T^2 rather than nT, which left the statistic sitting at the critical value: it rejected about a third of the time when no individual effect was present.

## Supported models

It accepts an `lm` and a `glm` with the Gaussian family and the identity link, unweighted
or with positive weights, a `fitWLS()` fit and, since 0.16.0, a rank-deficient fit, which it
tests on the estimable part of its design: it gives the value of the same model fitted without the
aliased columns. It refuses a `glm` of another family or link, a `survey::svyglm()` fit, a
fit with a zero weight, a coefficient that is not finite for another reason, and `data` that
lack rows or variables of the fit. The model is a pooled `lm` of the panel, with the units and
the periods as columns of `data`; a `plm::plm()` fit is not an `lm` and is refused.
Which model each test accepts, and why, is set out in [`test_results`](test_results.md), under
*Supported models*.

## References

Breusch, T. S., & Pagan, A. R. (1980). The Lagrange Multiplier Test and Its Applications to Model Specification in Econometrics. *Review of Economic Studies*, 47(1), 239–253.

## Examples

```r
 df <- data.frame(id = rep(1:5, each = 4), time = rep(1:4, 5), x = runif(20), y = rnorm(20))
 m <- lm(y ~ x, data = df)
 performBPRandomEffectsTest(m, df, "id")
```
